input.brief: Teaching dossier of a design professor: 48 studios, 3,922 contact hours, 2,737 students across 7 institutions in India, Canada, Singapore; making, creative code and AI

direction.name: The pinned poster
direction.idea: Something stays put while everything else changes. A title holds its place across the viewport and the images beneath it swap; the name is split to two opposite corners and the page passes between the halves; a single frame stays centred while its contents change. Every scroll step is a new cover of the same magazine. The idea suits subjects that are a series (a book of portraits, a line-up, a collection, a set of projects): the fixed element says what the series is, the changing element shows its members.
direction.composition: A sticky layer holds the fixed element for the height of two to three viewports: usually the title at 10–14vw across the middle or top of the screen, or two words pinned to the top-left and bottom-right corners. Under it, a stack of full-height panels scrolls by, each a single large photograph (portrait 4:5, centred, 40–50% of the viewport wide) with one line of caption at the same small size everywhere. The title sits above the images in the stacking order and uses `mix-blend-mode: difference` or a solid colour that reads on every panel. When the pinned run ends, the page releases into ordinary flowing sections with a narrow measure. Build with `position: sticky`; never hijack the scroll.
direction.typography: The pinned title is the only large type on the page. Captions and body share one small size (15–17px). Tight tracking and solid weight so the title reads over photographs.
direction.colour: One strong title colour against a pale or dark ground. Each panel may take its own flat ground colour sampled from its photograph.
direction.imagery: A series of photographs with the same crop ratio and the same framing (all portraits, all objects, all rooms), so that swapping them reads as one image changing. Five to eight in the pinned run.
direction.richness: Repetition with change. The fixed title makes each new photograph feel like an event, so the photographs must be good and consistent.
direction.pitfalls: If the title is not legible over every panel, the idea fails: test each one. Keep the pinned run under six viewports or it feels like a trap. On a phone the title shrinks to 16–18vw and stays pinned at the top; panels become full-width. A pin longer than three screens, or one where the screens under it are nearly empty, read in blind tests as a stuck page. Every screen under the pin needs its own content, and nothing may pass over the pinned words.

hero.name: Sentence split by a frame
hero.blueprint: A white or pale ground. One short sentence is broken in two and pushed to the edges: the first half flush to the 32px left margin, the second half flush to the right margin, both on the vertical centre line at clamp(40px, 3.6vw, 60px), medium weight. Between them, dead centre on columns 5–8, sits one media frame: 35% of the viewport wide, 16:9, corners 4px, holding a photograph or a working fragment of the product. The frame belongs to a vertical reel: the bottom 60px of the previous frame shows at the top edge of the viewport and the top 60px of the next at the bottom edge, same width, 24px gaps, so the centre column reads as a strip passing through the sentence. The stage is sticky; the reel advances three or four steps while the two halves of the sentence hold their place. Wordmark top-left; three text links and the single action as a small solid button top-right, all at 15px. Bottom-left on columns 1–4: one supporting sentence at 18px, its last line 32px above the bottom edge. The other corners stay empty.
hero.mobile: The halves stack: the first half of the sentence at 9vw flush left under the wordmark, then the frame at full width minus 16px margins and 4:3, then the second half flush right at 9vw. The neighbouring frames show as 28px slivers above and below. The supporting sentence and the action button follow at 16px. The links collapse to one word.
hero.headline: One sentence of four to six words split into two halves of up to about 14 characters each; the frame between them shows what it is about.

palette.name: Bottle green, gold
palette.note: Bottle green covers the page and warm gold sets all the type, with panels one step lighter than the ground. The button is solid gold with green text, and photographs are kept dark and warm so the pair is not disturbed.

motion.name: Pinned story
motion.description: One element holds its place with `position: sticky` (a title, a frame, a product fragment) while the items that belong to it scroll past or swap inside it. The page's ordinary scrolling does the work; nothing is hijacked. Hold it for about one screen per step and three screens at most, two held stages per page at most, with a line of text on every held screen. Recipe: 'Pinned story' in references/motion.md.

sections.name: Figure on the photograph's edge
sections.blueprint: One full-bleed photograph, 100vw by 88svh, and one figure set on it the way a film title sits on a frame. The figure, with its unit, is at clamp(120px, 17vw, 280px), leading 0.8, in paper colour, hugging the bottom-left corner with 24px margins, its baseline nearly on the photograph's lower edge. A neutral dark scrim covers only the bottom 35% of the image for legibility. On the same baseline at the right margin, right-aligned, a sentence of up to 26ch at 18px explains the figure. At the top-left, small at 20–24px, sits the heading of two to four words; the middle of the photograph stays clear. Two smaller supporting figures may follow below the photograph, on the ground: each at 40px with a one-line caption beside it, starting at columns 1 and 7, 40px under the image. Choose a figure that belongs to the picture: a height, a distance, a temperature, a year.
sections.mobile: The photograph is 80svh, cropped to its subject. The figure sits bottom-left at 30vw; the sentence moves above it at 16px, left-aligned. Supporting figures stack under the photograph at 32px, each with its caption on the line beneath.

sections.name: Pinned sentence, photographs pass
sections.blueprint: A wrapper 300svh tall. Inside it a `position: sticky; top: 0` layer of 100svh holds one sentence of 8–14 words, centred, three lines at clamp(36px, 4.6vw, 68px), leading 1.1, in a block 62% of the viewport wide. The sentence is a paragraph, not a heading; it is white with `mix-blend-mode: difference` (or a solid ink that reads over every photograph) and has a higher `z-index` than the images. Behind it, three photographs sit in normal flow at different sizes and sides and scroll past the fixed sentence: a 4:5 portrait 24vw wide with its left edge at 6vw; 70svh lower a 16:10 landscape 38vw wide touching the right margin; 70svh lower a 1:1 frame 18vw wide starting at 30vw. Each crosses the sentence once. When the wrapper ends, the sentence releases and scrolls away with the last photograph. No scroll hijacking.
sections.mobile: Wrapper 260svh. The sentence pins at 40% of the screen height at 8.4vw, four or five lines, with 20px margins. Photographs alternate: 64% wide on the left margin, 78% wide on the right margin, then 52% on the left, with 50svh between them.

sections.name: Line-up at one type size
sections.blueprint: A full-bleed flat section. The programme is a four-column table spanning the full width between 24px margins, with every cell at one size, clamp(20px, 2.1vw, 30px), one weight, no bold: the act or session flush left, the format starting at 33%, the room or stage at 66%, and the time range right-aligned at the far edge with tabular figures. Rows are 1.5em tall and separated by nothing but that leading; the fixed column starts do the organising. Day or part headings are a single line at the same size in the accent ink with 72px above and 20px below, and may be `position: sticky; top: 0` on a strip of the section's ground colour so the current day stays in view. Breaks and changeovers are rows set in capitals in the soft ink. There is no other heading. Comfortably holds 12–40 rows; with fewer than eight, raise the size to 3vw.
sections.mobile: Each entry becomes two lines: the act at 22px on the first, then format, room and time on one line at 14px in the soft ink with the time right-aligned. 18px between entries. Day headings stay sticky at the top on the ground colour.

sections.name: Pinned title, portraits pass
sections.blueprint: A wrapper tall enough for its portraits: about 90svh per person, up to six people. A `position: sticky; top: 0` layer of 100svh holds the heading, two words at clamp(88px, 12vw, 180px), leading 0.85, centred at mid-height, in white with `mix-blend-mode: difference` so it reads over ground and photographs alike. Beneath it in the stacking order, portraits scroll past in normal flow: each a 4:5 photograph 26–30vw wide, alternately starting at column 2 and ending at column 11, 60svh apart, so each one passes behind a different half of the heading. Under each portrait's left corner: the name at 18px, the role at 14px in the soft ink, and one sentence of up to 30 words in a 280px measure. The last portrait is followed by 40svh of empty ground before the heading releases. Square corners. Nothing else is on screen.
sections.mobile: The heading shrinks to 17vw and pins 16px from the top instead of at mid-height. Portraits become 72% wide, alternating between the left and right margins, 48px apart, each with name, role and sentence beneath at the portrait's width.

sections.name: Names passing a held square
sections.blueprint: A flat ground and one centred column of very large names: eight to fourteen project or product names in condensed capitals at clamp(96px, 14vw, 200px), leading 0.85, one per line and each line centred, so long names run nearly to the margins and short ones leave wide ground either side. A square frame 450px across (31vw), square corners, holds at the centre of the viewport behind the list: a sticky element (`position: sticky; top: calc(50svh - 225px)`) at the head of the list with a negative bottom margin equal to its height, centred, below the names in the stacking order, so the passing names cross the picture and are never hidden by it. Choose pictures with a calm centre, or lay a flat 30% scrim inside the frame, so the crossing name keeps 3:1. In the study the picture sits on top of the names; here nothing lies on top of large type. It shows the picture of whichever name is crossing its centre (an IntersectionObserver with a thin root margin at the viewport's middle sets the current name) and swaps with a 200ms crossfade. Level with the frame's middle, 48px to its left and right, two facts about the current item sit at 16px, the kind of work on the left and the year or price on the right, changing with it. The heading opens the list as its first line, at the same size in the soft ink, two words at most. Every name is a link. The section runs about three screens, so each name holds the centre for about a quarter of a screen.
sections.mobile: Names drop to 15vw and may wrap to two lines, still centred. The frame shrinks to a 60vw square and stays sticky at the centre; the two facts move into one row at 16px directly under it. The heading line stays first.

sections.name: Names running off the edges
sections.blueprint: A full-bleed band in a flat colour, about 34vh tall, holding a single line of names that is cropped by both viewport edges. The names are set at 8vw in the display weight, `white-space: nowrap`, separated by a solid round dot one third of the cap height, and the line moves slowly to the left (a CSS `translateX` animation over 40 seconds on a duplicated track, paused under `prefers-reduced-motion`). The band has no heading. Its meaning comes from one sentence at 18px set directly below the band at the left margin on the page ground, stating plainly who these names are. Supplied logos may replace names if all are available as single-colour SVGs at 0.8em height; do not mix logos and set names in one line. The band butts against the sections above and below with no gap.
sections.mobile: The band is 22vh tall with names at 15vw, still cropped at both edges and still moving. The explaining sentence sits under it at 16px with 20px margins. Do not add a second line running the opposite way; one line is the idea.

sections.name: Rising triptych
sections.blueprint: A wrapper about 200svh tall holds a sticky stage of 100svh on the plain page ground. The heading, two lines at clamp(32px, 2.8vw, 44px), is centred in the top fifth of the stage with one sentence at 17px under it. From the bottom edge three photographs rise as the page scrolls, each at its own speed. The centre one, a 4:5 portrait, starts 620px wide with only its top quarter showing and grows (scale and travel on a scroll-linked timeline) until it is about 760px wide with its top 40px below the sentence, cropped by the bottom edge, so it never reaches the heading. In the study it slides over the heading; here nothing lies on top of a heading. The two outer ones, each 360×530px, stand beside it with 10px gaps, their tops always 55px lower than the centre's, and by the end they are cut by the left and right viewport edges. Square corners, no captions, one consistent light across all three (warm interiors with warm, cold coast with cold). Under reduced motion show the end state with the heading above the three photographs.
sections.mobile: The centre portrait starts at 60% of the width and grows to nearly the full height; the outer two show as 40px slivers at the screen edges. The heading and sentence sit in the top third above it.

sections.name: Photograph half, menu half
sections.blueprint: A split footer one viewport tall. The left half is a single photograph filling columns 1–6 edge to edge, cropped hard by the left and bottom viewport edges: a close crop of the page's main subject, larger than it appeared anywhere above. The right half, on a flat field, is the site's menu set large: five or six section names stacked as links at about 2.6vw bold, 28px apart, starting at column 8 and 80px from the top. Rows are separated by space only; on hover a row's label shifts right by 12px and the others drop to the softer ink. Under the menu, 64px lower, two short blocks at 15px side by side: contact and social. The legal line runs along the very bottom of the right half at 12px. The wordmark sits small at the top of the right half, on the menu's left edge.
sections.mobile: The photograph leads at full width and 50svh, cropped tight. The menu follows on the flat field at 8vw per item with 20px between items, then contact and social stacked at 15px, then the legal line at 12px. The wordmark sits small above the menu.

references.name: City of Angels
references.idea: A fixed poster: the book title stays pinned across the viewport while portraits and press quotes swap underneath it, so every scroll step is a new cover.
references.hero: Pale icy-blue page. The title runs as one line of extra-bold uppercase grotesk at 10vw, centred, spanning about 82% of the width in saturated cyan, 120px from the top. A single portrait photograph, 37% of the viewport wide and nearly full height, is centred beneath; the title crosses over its upper quarter, so the middle letters sit on the image. The author name sits top-centre in small bold caps, a two-bar menu icon top-right. Bottom-left, a 13-line bold paragraph in a narrow 340px column; bottom-right, a solid black five-point star about 70px wide.
references.type: ABC Diatype throughout: weight 800 uppercase for the 144px title, bold copy around 20-24px with leading near 1.0; Founders Grotesk Mono in tiny caps for quote attributions. Two sizes plus a label. The final frame catches title letters slanting to oblique.
references.colour: #e4f8fd #06aeef #0a0a0a #c8b59d — The page colour is a pale tint of the title's cyan; cyan appears only on the title, the opening words and quotation marks. Text and star are black. The digest records one solid cyan section.
references.imagery: Full-length street-style portraits, all vertical at about 2:3, saturated natural light, subject standing centre. One image at a time, square corners, centred on the page with the title overprinting it.
references.layout: One pinned composition repeated for seven screens: central image column, fixed title, and a single text block that alternates between the left and right gutters and shifts height each step. Margins about 46px; nothing else on screen.

sections.description: Each scroll step keeps the pinned title and swaps the central portrait. One press quote sits in a column 180-340px wide in an outer gutter, alternating right, left, right, and placed at a different height each time (upper, middle, lower). Quotes are bold black with tight leading and cyan quotation marks; the source follows in tiny underlined or mono caps. The black star stays bottom-right and is caught at different rotation angles.

Not captured in the shots, but the digest records four stacked, centred, uppercase links at 144px (10vw) in the same extra-bold grotesk, plus a solid cyan section: navigation reuses the title's exact type size, one link per line, so the menu is another poster rather than a small list.

steal: Pin one giant title across the viewport and let a single centred image change beneath it, with the type overprinting the photo's top quarter.
Use a pale tint of the accent colour as the page background so the saturated title and the background read as one hue.
Give each scroll step one text block and move it between left and right gutters at varying heights instead of stacking sections.

references.name: NORMAL IS BORING
references.idea: The brand name is split and half of it turned upside down: a plain sans first word top-left and a serif last word flipped 180 degrees bottom-right stay fixed while panels slide sideways between them.
references.hero: A white panel fills the left 80%; a full-height interior photo takes the right 20%. Top-left: the first word of the name in light geometric capitals, about 56px. Bottom-right of the white panel: an italic 'is' above the last word in bold didone, rotated 180 degrees so it reads upside down. Three small caps nav links run vertically up the panel's right edge. The 50px headline is broken into three two-line fragments on different columns and baselines: one at 21% from the left, one a line lower at 42%, one back at 21% whose last word turns bold italic didone. A seven-line 13px paragraph hangs beneath the middle fragment.
references.type: Izmir, a light geometric sans in capitals, for wordmark, hero fragments and 13px body; Juana, a high-contrast didone, bold italic for accent words and huge roman capitals (10-12vw and larger, cropped) for scrolling statements; Editorial New ultralight for the reversed paragraph.
references.colour: #ffffff #000000 #ece4da #c7d7e9 #db5c59 #1f9aa0 — White and black panels alternate with warm beige; pale blue and coral panels appear deeper in. Type stays black or white. A single teal dot acts as cursor; photos bring wood and plant tones.
references.imagery: Warm interior and garden photography of finished homes in natural light, wood and linen tones. Square-cornered; used as full-height strips, full-bleed panels and smaller insets laid over larger photos by about a third.
references.layout: Reads as a sideways journey: white, black and beige panels slide horizontally with photos and oversized words cropped by panel edges. Text fragments sit on an irregular grid; the two halves of the logo stay fixed in opposite corners.

sections.description: The photo strip from the hero grows to a full-height panel while a second, smaller interior photo slides over it, overlapping by roughly a third. To the right a white panel carries a four-line statement in didone capitals about 90px tall, set so the lines run off the panel edge and are completed only as scrolling continues. A small 12px paragraph sits under the statement's left edge.

Full black panel. A nine-line paragraph in an ultralight serif at about 32px starts 70% of the way across and runs off the right edge; its words fade from white through grey to near-black line by line as a scroll-driven reveal. A single photo of a pool at dusk, roughly 300px square, sits alone in the lower-left third. The menu pill and flipped logo invert to white.

Values panel on beige. Along the left edge a vertical ticker repeats one word in 90px didone capitals rotated 90 degrees, separated by thin eight-point asterisks. Beside it a large exterior photograph of a stone-and-glass house with a bathroom photo about half its size laid over its lower-right corner, square edges, no shadow or border.

Beige panel where the project title is set so large that single didone letters exceed the viewport height and are cropped top and bottom, acting as black shapes in the left half. In the right half a modest 300px-wide aerial photo floats with a bracketed year above and a centred serif caption and two-line descriptor below.

steal: Split a two-part brand name into opposite corners of the viewport and flip one half 180 degrees so the logo enacts the name.
Break a headline into fragments on different columns and baselines, like a stair, and hang the body paragraph under one fragment only.
Scale a project title until single letters are taller than the viewport, then float a small captioned photo beside those cropped shapes.
references.media: The only picture on the first screen is an interior photograph cropped to the right 20% (290px, full height), the leading edge of a pinned horizontal track that widens to about 65% on the next screen. Inside the track, overlapping pairs lay a smaller photograph over a larger full-height one, project cards widen as they reach the centre, and a photograph sits framed in a flat coral field; all 29 images have square corners and reveal by clip-path while scaling down from 1.5, and there is no video.
references.motion: About 2.5s of entrance: the logo, then headline characters, then body lines rising from masks (y over 0.65-0.97s power3.out at a 0.025-0.033 stagger), then the photo and nav. One section pins for +=1150% (about 10,350px) at scrub 1 and is translated sideways; photo pairs move on scrub 0.35, a statement fills line by line on scrub 0, and project cards widen over 1s power1.inOut; a dot cursor grows with a back-out overshoot the house layer does not use.

references.name: Lorenzo Bocchi – Shot on iPhone
references.idea: Black-and-white phone photographs fly through dark 3D space as a twisting ribbon, and the viewer chooses how the archive is arranged (reel, wall, trail, drift; flow, grid, map).
references.hero: Pure black canvas filling the viewport. A diagonal helix of portrait photo cards runs from upper-left to lower-right: four cards near the centre are lit and legible (each about 200 by 280px, slightly rounded corners, each rotated a little further around the axis), while cards above and below fade to dark grey blanks curling away. Behind them a single word in ultra-bold condensed caps spans 80% of the width, its letters half the viewport tall, in a grey only a few points lighter than the background. Four pill-shaped control groups sit in the corners: menu label top-left, three view modes top-right, two round icon buttons bottom-left, four layout modes bottom-right.
references.type: GeistSans around 14px inside the pill controls is the only readable text. The giant background word is ultra-bold condensed caps roughly 440px tall, used as texture at near-zero contrast. No headings or captions.
references.colour: #000000 #191919 #262626 #383838 #e6e6e6 — Black and greys only; the photographs are all monochrome, so the brightest values on the page are image highlights. Controls are dark grey capsules with a black active segment.
references.imagery: Black-and-white travel and street photographs, all portrait, with a soft vignette, mapped onto slightly curved cards in WebGL; only cards near the focal plane are lit, the rest fall into darkness.
references.layout: One fixed viewport with no document flow. Content floats in the centre 50% of the screen; interface is pushed to the four corners with 16px insets, leaving edges and middle free for the image stream.

sections.description: Scrolling does not move a page; it advances the ribbon. In each frame three or four cards occupy a diagonal band through the centre, the middle one facing the viewer and neighbours rotated progressively edge-on, like prints on a spiral staircase. Cards leaving focus darken to charcoal silhouettes that continue the curve toward the top-left and bottom-right corners, so the path stays readable even when the images are not.

Navigation is four floating capsules rather than a bar. Each is a dark-grey rounded container; multi-option ones hold a black pill behind the active word, giving three view modes and four layout modes as segmented switches. On mobile the two top capsules sit side by side, the bottom ones merge into one row, and their text scales up to thumb size.

steal: Set a single giant word behind the content at two or three percent contrast so it reads as depth, not as a headline.
Light only the items near the focal point and let the rest fall to dark silhouettes that still trace the path.
Put controls in four corner capsules with a sliding active pill, keeping the whole centre free for content.
